title: EARS: Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling in Large-scale Multi-Agent Systems
title_zh: EARS：面向大规模多智能体系统中可靠子智能体建模的可解释拒答
abstract_en: In large-scale enterprise settings, centralized multi-agent systems (MAS) are increasingly adopted, in which a coordinator delegates user requests to lightweight, domain-specialized sub-agents. While this architecture improves modularity, scalability, and cost efficiency, its reliability depends not only on accurate routing but also on sub-agents' ability to calibrate their responses to capability constraints. In particular, sub-agents built on smaller fine-tuned models often struggle with such calibration, leading them to over-answer ambiguous, underspecified, misrouted, or unsupported requests and produce hallucinated outputs instead of actionable feedback. To address this challenge, we present EARS (Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling), a production-oriented framework that reframes sub-agent abstention as an inter-agent communication protocol: a sub-agent does not merely abstain, but exposes an actionable failure state to the coordinator. EARS curates human-agent interaction data using an ensemble of calibrated LLM-as-a-Judge models, producing structured abstention labels and rationales under a taxonomy of sub-agent failure modes. These data are used to fine-tune sub-agents to detect failure conditions and return rationales for coordinator-level clarification, rerouting, or fallback. We evaluate EARS in a large-scale production e-commerce assistant supporting enterprise business intelligence workflows. EARS improves the overall response pass rate from 68.5% to 78.9%, demonstrating that sub-agent-side explanatory abstention improves MAS reliability.
abstract_zh: 在大规模企业场景中，集中式 Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) 正被广泛采用：由一个 coordinator 将用户请求分发给轻量、面向特定领域的 sub-agents。该架构提升了模块化、可扩展性与成本效率，但其可靠性不仅依赖准确路由，也依赖 sub-agents 能否根据自身能力边界校准回答。尤其是基于较小 fine-tuned models 的 sub-agents，常在面对模糊、信息不足、误路由或不支持的请求时过度作答，产生幻觉而非提供可操作反馈。为此，论文提出 EARS (Explanatory Abstention for Reliable Sub-Agent Modeling)，将 sub-agent 的 abstention 重新定义为一种 inter-agent communication protocol：sub-agent 不只是拒答，而是向 coordinator 暴露可操作的失败状态。EARS 使用一组 calibrated LLM-as-a-Judge models 构建 human-agent interaction data，在子智能体失败模式分类体系下生成结构化 abstention labels 与 rationales，并用这些数据微调 sub-agents，使其能够检测失败条件并返回理由，供 coordinator 进行澄清、重路由或 fallback。作者在支持企业商业智能工作流的大规模生产级 e-commerce assistant 中评估 EARS，使整体 response pass rate 从 68.5% 提升到 78.9%，表明子智能体侧的可解释拒答能提升 MAS 可靠性。
key_points_zh: 提出 EARS，将 sub-agent abstention 从简单拒答升级为面向 coordinator 的可操作失败状态报告，用于澄清、重路由或 fallback。
针对企业级集中式 MAS 中常见的子智能体过度回答问题，重点处理模糊、信息不足、误路由和能力不支持等失败模式。
使用 calibrated LLM-as-a-Judge ensemble 自动标注 human-agent interaction data，生成结构化拒答标签与解释理由。
通过 fine-tuning 训练轻量 sub-agents 识别自身能力边界，并返回 rationale，从而改善跨智能体协作与系统级决策。
在生产级 e-commerce assistant 的企业商业智能场景中，EARS 将整体 response pass rate 从 68.5% 提升至 78.9%。

llm_assessment.comment: A useful production-oriented multi-agent reliability framework for an e-commerce assistant, but it is more about enterprise agent robustness than commerce-specific search or recommendation.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该论文面向电商助手中的多智能体可靠性问题，具备实用价值，但更偏企业级智能体稳健性而非电商搜索推荐核心问题。
